correctness.rationale: Let I_n be disjoint successive blocks of size m_n=max(1,ceil(c log_2(n+1))) and lambda_n=n/(n+1). Row sums lambda_n<1 prove non-attainment of T on c0; the disjoint ℓ1 action has norm ∑lambda_n|y_n|<∥y∥_1 for every nonzero y, so the first adjoint does not attain. T**1 has norm one. For iid signs with favored probability q=max(p,1−p), each row is a binomial m_n mean, independent across n. Binomial Chernoff upper bounds and one-binomial-mass lower bounds give n^(−c D_2(r∥q)) up to logarithmic factors; independent Borel–Cantelli proves limsup |row mean|=2R(c,q)−1, R=1 at/below c_*=1/(-log_2q), otherwise D_2(R∥q)=1/c. Multiplying by lambda_n does not change the limsup, and dist(z,c0)=limsup|z_n|. If this is less than one, finitely many initial rows also have modulus <1, giving nonattainment for typical signs. Norming-sign set is the intersection of open dense late-block events, and a zero-density forced sequence of constant blocks gives a full-dimension Cantor subset. At c=c_* the all-favored-block probabilities have divergent sum, so equality case is included. These prove the exact fixed-operator category/measure distinction for every c>0 and p∈(0,1); finite diagnostics alone do not prove any almost-sure claim.
